summary: Specifies how an LDP speaker can signal that it has finished its initial label advertisements after a session starts. Without this, a peer cannot know when it has received all labels. It is a Proposed Standard.

eli5.summary: When a friend is reading you a long list, it helps to hear 'that's all.' This gives routers a way to say it.

questions: how does ldp signal label advertisement completion
what is end of lib in ldp
what is the unrecognized notification capability
subtitle: How an LDP router tells its peer that it has finished sending its initial labels.

tldr.problem: After an LDP session starts, a speaker cannot tell when its peer has advertised all of its labels, because the LDP specification has no way to signal completion.
tldr.mechanism: A speaker sends a Notification message carrying the End-of-LIB status code and a Typed Wildcard FEC, but only to peers that advertised the new Unrecognized Notification capability at session setup.
tldr.outcome: Features such as LDP-IGP synchronization, LDP graceful restart and wildcard label requests get a definite signal instead of a guess. It is a Proposed Standard.

today: RFC 5919 is a Proposed Standard published in August 2010. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The Missing 'That's All'
sections.content:
After an LDP session is established, it is often useful for a speaker to know when its peer has advertised all labels from its Label Information Base (LIB). Examples are LDP-IGP synchronization (RFC 5443) and re-establishing a session under LDP Graceful Restart (RFC 3478). The LDP specification (RFC 5036) has no mechanism for a speaker to say it has completed its initial label advertisements.

RFC 5919 uses a Notification message with a new End-of-LIB status code for this. Because RFC 5036 does not define how a speaker treats a status code it does not understand, the RFC also uses the LDP capability mechanism (RFC 5561) so a speaker can announce at session setup that it can handle such a notification.

The mechanism is considered useful for the Downstream Unsolicited advertisement mode. It is not useful for Downstream on Demand, since the speaker requests particular bindings and knows when it has them.
sections.eli5: Two routers swap lists of labels. Right now neither can tell when the other list has ended, so this adds a way to say 'done.'

sections.title: The Unrecognized Notification Capability
sections.content:
A speaker MAY include a Capability Parameter in its Initialization message to say that it ignores Notification messages whose Status TLV carries a non-fatal status code it does not know. The capability is a TLV of type 0x0603. The U-bit MUST be 1, the F-bit MUST be 0, and the S-bit MUST be 1 to show the capability is being advertised.

When a speaker receives a Notification with an unrecognized status code, it MAY write a console or system log message for troubleshooting.
sections.eli5: Before telling a secret code word, you check that your friend knows to shrug at words they do not understand, instead of getting upset.

sections.title: Signaling Completion
sections.content:
A conforming speaker SHOULD signal completion of its label advertisements by sending a Notification, if the peer advertised the Unrecognized Notification capability. It SHOULD send it for each FEC type, even when it has zero label bindings to advertise. The Notification MUST carry:

  • a Status TLV, with the E- and F-bits zero, holding the End-of-LIB status code 0x0000002F;
  • a FEC TLV with the Typed Wildcard FEC Element (RFC 5918) that names the FEC type whose initial advertisements are complete.

A speaker MUST NOT send End-of-LIB to a peer that has not advertised the capability. This applies to peers found by either basic or extended discovery.
sections.eli5: When a router has said everything it wanted to say about one kind of label, it sends a short 'finished with this kind' message, even if it had nothing to say.

sections.title: When the Notification Never Arrives
sections.content:
There is no guarantee that a speaker will receive an End-of-LIB Notification, even if it signaled the capability. Supporting the capability does not make it mandatory to send or receive End-of-LIB. A speaker simply ignores a notification with a status code it does not support.

To cope, a speaker MAY time out waiting. It SHOULD start a per-peer EOL Notification timer right after session establishment, with a RECOMMENDED default of 60 seconds that SHOULD be configurable. Each later label advertisement resets the timer, and the End-of-LIB Notification stops it. If the timer expires, the speaker behaves as if it had received End-of-LIB. A notification that arrives after expiry SHOULD be ignored.
sections.eli5: If you wait a minute and your friend says nothing more, you decide the list is over and move on.

sections.title: Where End-of-LIB Helps
sections.content:
Which bindings count as 'all' is a judgment call for the speaker, since known FECs and labels change over time. It can depend on the label distribution control mode, the FECs with local labels, and configuration that limits what it may advertise.

  • LDP-IGP Sync: without End-of-LIB the speaker relies on a heuristic, which may signal the IGP too soon (more dropped traffic) or too late (traffic stays on sub-optimal paths). With it, the speaker can treat LDP as fully operational on the link and have the IGP advertise the link with normal cost.
  • LDP Graceful Restart: receiving End-of-LIB lets a speaker stop using stale forwarding state from that peer and recover resources without waiting for the time period to expire. That expiry still applies if the notification does not arrive.
  • Wildcard Label Request: after answering a Label Request for a Typed Wildcard FEC, the speaker should send End-of-LIB for that FEC type, removing uncertainty for the requester.
sections.eli5: Knowing the list is finished lets a router start using a new road at the right moment, throw away old maps sooner, or know a request was fully answered.

sections.title: Security and IANA
sections.content:
The RFC says no security considerations apply beyond those of base LDP (RFC 5036), further described in RFC 5920.

IANA assigned the End-of-LIB status code 0x0000002F from the IETF Consensus region of the Status Code name space, and the Unrecognized Notification capability 0x0603 from the IETF Consensus range of the TLV Type name space.
sections.eli5: It reuses the same safety rules as the rest of LDP, and the official registry now lists the two new code numbers.
